comment: The draft addresses open standards, model substitutability, national control and vendor lock-in. Whole-life assurance would be stronger if it explicitly covered not only technical data portability but semantic portability, continuity of governed content, supplier exit and decommissioning. A country may possess its data but still be unable to interpret or safely migrate it if models, bindings, transformation logic or audit history are proprietary or incomplete.

public.text: The draft addresses open standards, model substitutability, national control and vendor lock-in. Whole-life assurance would be stronger if it explicitly covered not only technical data portability but semantic portability, continuity of governed content, supplier exit and decommissioning. A country may possess its data but still be unable to interpret or safely migrate it if models, bindings, transformation logic or audit history are proprietary or incomplete.
public.suggestedRevision: Add procurement and lifecycle requirements for open/documented interfaces; export of data together with metadata, terminology versions and logical-model identifiers; portability of audit and provenance records; supplier performance and renewal checkpoints; cybersecurity patching; source-code escrow where proportionate; migration and decommissioning plans; continuity during supplier failure; and reassessment when contracts, models or intended uses materially change. Require semantic as well as technical portability.
